title: Cascade Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Cascade Health onboarding to Redwood Inference. Covered account goals, timelines, networking/security requirements for Private deployment, initial pilot scope, and next steps for documentation, benchmarks, and pricing. Action items assigned for network diagrams, SSO details, and a smoke-test plan.
topics: Network/VPC and KMS requirements for Private deployment
Pilot scope: endpoints, throughput targets, sample prompts
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding checklist and network diagram template (Jordan) by 2027-04-14
Cascade to share SSO/SAML metadata and KMS contacts (Evan) by 2027-04-16
Schedule pilot kickoff/benchmarks with SE (Samir) for week of 2027-04-26
action_items: Owner: Jordan Mills | Item: Send onboarding checklist & sample network diagram | Due: 2027-04-14
Owner: Evan Park | Item: Share SSO/SAML metadata and KMS contact | Due: 2027-04-16
Owner: Samir Patel | Item: Draft pilot test plan (throughput/latency/quality) | Due: 2027-04-20
Owner: Sofia Delgado | Item: Provide internal firewall rules & bastion info | Due: 2027-04-18
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, from Redwood side we've got Priya and Samir and I'm Jordan, I'll kick things off. Good to meet you all.
[00:14] Marta Ruiz: Hey Jordan, thanks, Marta here. We have Tom, Sofia and Evan on our side. Excited to get started.
[00:28] Jordan Mills: Quick agenda — intro, goals for the integration, security and networking constraints for the Private deployment, pilot scope and timelines, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:38] Tom Bennett: Yep that's great. Our top-level goal is to get the search and triage assistant into prod for a subset of clinics by Q3. We need sub-second median latency for small queries and predictable cost.
[00:52] Priya Nair: Helpful. When you say sub-second, is that 95th perc or median?
[00:56] Tom Bennett: 95th perc ideally, <500ms end-to-end for the most common prompts.
[01:03] Samir Patel: Okay noted — we'll size the pilot around that. Quick clarifying question on data residency, Marta? Are you requiring on-prem or is VPC in a cloud region fine?
[01:14] Marta Ruiz: VPC in a cloud region is fine, but all PHI must remain in our account and keys must be customer-managed — so KMS/HSM integration is required.
[01:25] Evan Park: Also need SOC 2 plus logs routed to our SIEM; audit trails for prompts stored for 90 days. RBAC for console access and SAML-based SSO.
[01:36] Jordan Mills: That's totally in line with our Redwood Private offering. We support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering or private link. We'll provide audit logs and can ship logs to your SIEM via S3 or direct ingestion. For RBAC and SSO we integrate with SAML/OIDC and support SCIM for provisioning.
[01:54] Sofia Delgado: On the networking side we prefer only outbound from our infra to Redwood, we have strict inbound policies. How does the onboarding network look?
[02:03] Samir Patel: For Private, typically we establish a peered VPC or PrivateLink endpoint. There are two common patterns — peered VPC with route tables and security groups, or a transit gateway pattern. We'll share a sample network diagram.
[02:16] Jordan Mills: We'll send the network template after the call. It lists ports, CIDR ranges, and expected NAT/bastion requirements.
[02:23] Tom Bennett: Great. Pilot scope — what are our options for model variants and cost controls? We don't want surprises.
[02:31] Priya Nair: For pilots we usually run a controlled workload against a curated model that matches capability needs — we can propose an open model or quantized variant. Redwood Optimize will provide batching and quantization recommendations to hit cost targets while meeting latency SLOs.
[02:46] Tom Bennett: Is there an option to auto-fallback to a cheaper model if load spikes?
[02:50] Samir Patel: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible variant — we can define policies per route. For mission-critical routes you can pin versions.
[02:59] Marta Ruiz: What about evaluation — we need to track quality regressions and have a regression alert tied to our test prompts.
[03:06] Priya Nair: We'll onboard your eval set into our quality monitoring. We can set baselines and alert on regressions, that ties into rollout policies so we can block a rollout if quality drops.
[03:17] Evan Park: For encryption, KMS in our account is required. Also we need TDE for storage and proofs for key rotation policy.
[03:25] Jordan Mills: We support customer keys and can document rotation windows; Samir will include the KMS integration steps in the security addendum.
[03:34] Sofia Delgado: From ops, our initial ask — can you run a smoke test that simulates our request shape? We have lots of short prompts and a few long summaries.
[03:45] Samir Patel: Yep, that's the standard pilot. We'll need sample prompts and the expected distribution (percentiles of length). We'll run throughput/latency benchmarks and share the spreadsheet.
[03:55] Tom Bennett: Timeline question — what does onboarding usually take? Our target is pilot start in late April and production by early July.
[04:02] Priya Nair: That timeline is doable. Typical onboarding for Private with a pilot is 4–8 weeks depending on network and security approvals. If you get the SSO/KMS and firewall info in the next two weeks we can hit your dates.
[04:15] Marta Ruiz: Okay we'll prioritize.
[04:18] Jordan Mills: I'll put key milestones in an onboarding checklist — discovery, network setup, pilot benchmarks, rollout planning, SLA and pricing review.
[04:27] Evan Park: Can you share your SOC 2 report and any pen test summaries?
[04:31] Jordan Mills: Yes we'll share SOC 2 attestation and a security pack with our controls and pen test overview. I'll drop those after the call.
[04:39] Sofia Delgado: Any gotchas we should be aware of? For example, kv cache behavior or long context costs?
[04:45] Samir Patel: Good point — long context windows do increase token costs and some kernels have different perf characteristics. We'll recommend a quantization profile and batching settings to balance latency and cost. Also prefix/KV caching can drastically reduce costs for repeated prompts.
[04:57] Tom Bennett: Pricing conversation — can you send a pilot pricing sheet?
[05:00] Priya Nair: Yes, Jordan will share the pilot pricing tiers and an estimate model. For Dedicated or Reserved capacity we'll include committed discount options.
[05:10] Jordan Mills: Recap: Jordan sends onboarding checklist, network diagram, SOC2/security pack; Samir drafts pilot test plan and benchmark spreadsheet; Evan shares SSO/KMS metadata; Sofia shares firewall rules. We agreed to target pilot kickoff week of 2027-04-26.
[05:28] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:31] Jordan Mills: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot and the security review. Bye.
[05:36] End of recording
